Hi Soojin,

Sorry for the radio silence — we had an unexpected maintenance window at our primary DC that forced the team offline for the slot this morning. Really sorry about the no-show.

We'd still like to run the hands-on session. Our core ask: a prompt review (40–45m) and then an extended load window. For the load portion we'll need about 60–75 minutes total (30m ramp, 30m peak, 15m cool-down). Our SREs prefer late-afternoon CET slots.

Open slots from our side next week:
- Tue 2027-06-22: 16:00–18:00 CEST
- Wed 2027-06-23: 18:00–20:00 CEST
- Thu 2027-06-24: 08:00–10:00 CEST (if you need an early window)

If you can confirm a time and which of your engineers will lead the load test, we'll invite our SRE and a security rep. Also if you have a short async runbook we can read ahead of the session, that would help.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Platform Eng — Acme Corp

Quick plan:

- Marissa will run the load test and lead the runtime tuning during the session (GPU orchestration & pre-warm).
- Priyom will handle the prompt review and prepare a short prompt checklist so we can validate output quality before the load ramp.

Two questions before I lock a slot:
1) Can Marissa get GPU access for a 75-minute continuous window on Tue 6/22 at 16:00 CEST? We have burst commitments on that day — if not, Marissa notes a 18:00 CEST option.
2) Do you want us to run the full 60–75m as one contiguous window, or split into a 45m ramp/validation + 30m peak (we can do either; splitting helps with SLO risk).

I've attached a short async runbook and our standard load script template to this thread so your SREs can review.

Attachments: redwood-poc-async-runbook.pdf, acme-loadtest-script.yaml

If that looks good I'll propose Tue 2027-06-22 16:00 CEST and send the invite subject to Marissa confirming GPU availability.

Thanks,
— Soojin

My preference is 18:00 CEST to avoid risk of throttling mid-test. I'll prepare a short ops checklist (pre-warm KV cache, disable autoscaling during peak, continuous batching profile: medium) and post it here once ready.
